Title: Qud Expanded Community Edition
Description:
[h1]Qud Expanded Community Edition[/h1]
[i]A community-maintained fork of [b]Caves of Qud Expanded[/b] by Mura.[/i]

This is a [b]separate mod[/b]. It does not replace, modify, or take over the original, which remains Mura's and is still available here:
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1134036260]Caves of Qud Expanded[/url]

[h1]Development notes[/h1]
[list]
[*]I, VixyGrey, do use AI to help me with development and documentation tasks.
[*]I am actively developing this mod, adding new features, fixing bugs, and addressing feedback.
[/list]

This mod exists because of other people's work. Please give them the credit.

[list]
[*][b]Mura[/b] (@mura_raven) — created Caves of Qud Expanded and spent years on it. This fork is their mod, continued.
[*][b]Noble Lark[/b] (a.k.a. [b]chirps[/b]) — all 18 psionic subtype sprites. Mura named him specifically when opening the mod up, and that credit is permanent here.

Mura opened the mod to the community asking one thing: give credit where due. That is permanent here.

[h1]What the mod does[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Psionic Adept[/b] — a third genotype, 18 subtypes, casters and martial guardians.
[*][b]Psionic chips[/b] — 144 implantable chips granting real mutations to genotypes that cannot mutate. All of them can be found.
[*][b]Complete weapon and armor families[/b] — bronze to zetachrome, one- and two-handed, consistent stats and prices.
[*][b]New weapon classes[/b] — katanas, rapiers, halberds, greataxes, greatswords, war hammers, wristblades and more.
[*][b]Skill and economy retuning[/b], and a home base building in Joppa.
[/list]

[h1]Compatibility[/h1]
[b]Do not enable this and the original Caves of Qud Expanded at the same time.[/b] Pick one. A continuation defines the same things the original does — 36 script types with the same names — so Qud reports a type conflict and whichever loads first wins. Saves do not carry across either.

[b]The Grand Bazaar[/b] and [b]Experience Curve Beta[/b] are both fine alongside this. Verified by comparing every object, table and script type the three declare — a record-level check rather than a play-test, so please report anything you hit.

Every change this fork makes to a vanilla record is a merge, never a replacement. It does not overwrite vanilla data and should not discard what future Qud patches add. It should also play nice with most other mods. Please report any compatibility issues to me, either via Steam or via an Issue on GitHub.

[h1]New features[/h1]
[b]Eleven options, in Qud's own options menu under Mods.[/b] Each defaults to what the mod has always done, except where marked.

[list]
[*][b]Mutation points[/b] — the mod's 16 against vanilla's 12, or anything from 0 to 24
[*][b]Mutant hit points per level[/b] — 1-5, 2-3 (what 2.2 shipped), or vanilla's 1-4
[*][b]Extra skill points per level[/b] — 65 and 85, against vanilla's 50 and 70
[*][b]Extra starting skills[/b] — Staunch Wounds, Cooking and Gathering, Meal Preparation, Menacing Stare
[*][b]Eased skill requirements[/b] — Axe and Cudgel on Strength [i]or[/i] Agility, and lower numbers for Long Blade, Multiweapon Fighting and Tinkering
[*][b]Retuned skill point costs[/b] — free Disassemble, dearer Reverse Engineer, Butchery and Spicer
[*][b]Starting reputation bonus[/b] — +300 with Joppa. [b]Off by default[/b]: power with no content attached is a thing to ask for
[*][b]Home base building in Joppa[/b] — bed, storage, oven, becoming nook
[*][b]Psionic chips in loot[/b] — off closes the supply completely, since no chip is tinkerable
[*][b]Your own Chip Interface slots[/b] — 1 for a mutant, 2 for a True Kin
[*][b]Chip Interface slots on other humanoids[/b] — nothing here ever fills them
[/list]

Psionic Adepts are unaffected throughout: their numbers are the genotype, not an addition to a vanilla one. Chips in loot and skill costs apply immediately; hit points and skill points from your next level; eased requirements after a restart; the rest at chargen.

[b]Six effect arrows, back from a file that was entirely commented out[/b] — blaze (heat), cryo (cold), dream dew (sleep gas), hulk honey (mires what it hits and drags fliers down), starshell (flashbang) and stinger (poison gas).

[b]Four effect shotgun shells[/b] — incendiary, cryo, flechette (punches through armor) and takedown (knocks targets off their feet and grounds fliers), for the pump shotgun, combat shotgun, drum shotgun and modified handcannon. They drop from Ammo 2 upward and are craftable once you find the disk.

[h1]Tweaks and fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]All 144 psionic chips can be found now.[/b] The chip tables listed the first chip of each family and its chipset, and since no chip is tinkerable, the other 72 had no way of reaching you. They are in the tables now. How often a chip drops at all is unchanged.
[*][b]Ten more items are findable[/b] — the nanoweave and flexi sets, the mutating mask and the iron maceth, each placed in the drop table matching its own tier. The empty armor rack, which had never been given a spot anywhere, now stands with its siblings in the Joppa building.
[*][b]Mutated Humans gain 1-5 hit points per level[/b], which is what the mod's own notes have always described. The XML had 2-3, which averages out to the same as vanilla. If you prefer 2-3, it is one of the options.
[*][b]High-tier armor drops cascade again.[/b] Four tables replaced vanilla's tier cascade rather than adding to it, which made a tier-8 roll produce zetachrome every time. The mod's own zetachrome carries the weight now instead, landing at 25%.
[*][b]Stats and prices settled[/b] on nine items, the dark matter cell and the wristblade family, so each sits where its tier and its family would put it. The artifact tables and both recoilers now merge with vanilla's records rather than standing in for them.
[*][b]The advanced hoversled floats and the sphere of negative weight is a trinket again[/b] — a one-letter typo had kept both tags from applying. Spotted and fixed by Jah-yee.
[*][b]Multiweapon Fighting no longer offers Akimbo.[/b] It shared a single implementation with the Pistol tree's copy, so the mod's version stood in wherever the game asked for vanilla's — most visibly on the [b]Gunslinger[/b] calling. Akimbo is untouched where it has always lived, and Multiweapon Fighting keeps its reduced requirements.
[/list]

The full list, with the reasoning behind each, is in the changelog on GitHub.

[h1]Version and saves[/h1]
[b]2.4.0.[/b] Loads on 2.3.x saves — this update needs no new character. See [b]Known issues[/b] for two caveats.

Coming from Mura's original, [b]start a new character[/b]: identifiers changed during the fork, and Qud writes those into save files.

[h1]Known issues[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]The quill arrow is disabled.[/b] It shipped in 2.3.0 with a bleed that could never fire — bleeding is melee-only in Qud, and an arrow is not a melee weapon. The hulk honey arrow takes its place. Quill arrows you already have still fire; they no longer drop.
[*][b]Effect shells need a shotgun obtained after updating.[/b] A gun already in your save keeps the shot it was built with, so the new shells do nothing in it. Any shotgun you pick up or build from now on works.
[/list]
